{"hookSpecificOutput":{"hookEventName":"SessionStart","additionalContext":"# Loaded from memory (Tier 0 — core.md, user-level):

# Core Memory — ZCode (user-level, always-on)

## Follow-up work covenant (NON-NEGOTIABLE — all repos)
- Nothing identified during a PR/issue closeout is silently dropped. EVERY
  unfixed item — finding, residual, disclosed limitation, flake, hardening idea —
  gets exactly ONE recorded disposition in the closure ledger:
  - FIX-NOW: the PR introduced it (mandatory), or it is small and in this PR's
    files and scope.
  - ABSORB: an open issue already covers it -> comment on that issue, no new one.
  - FILE: it passes the necessity gate below.
  - RECORD: it fails gate 1 or 2, or the user declined it -> one row (item, reason, re-evaluation trigger) in
    the PR body's "Considered, not filed" table. RECORD is a complete closure.
  - ASK: it needs a product/maintainer decision, OR it fails only gate 3 ->
    ask the user; file nothing yet. ASK beats FIX-NOW when the fix needs a
    product/compatibility decision. Decline -> RECORD (quote it); approval ->
    FILE (gate-3/Improvement), fix in-PR + restart Stage A (gate-4), or back to
    investigation (unverified; never file an INFERENCE).
- Necessity gate — FILE only if ALL hold: (1) VERIFIED by an executed probe or
  exact source trace (INFERENCE never files); (2) a concrete reachable trigger
  with a correctness, safety/security, data-loss, or workflow-blocking
  consequence (coverage/docs/wording/"could harden" fail unless they hide a real
  defect); (3) material (hot path, invalidates a gate/contract, or blocks planned
  work); (4) not already tracked and not fixable in this PR. Failing gate 4
  means ABSORB (tracked) or ASK to fix a pre-existing item in-PR, never RECORD. A wedge/fail-open/security/data-loss
  consequence satisfies gate 3 automatically. Never RECORD a verified,
  consequential defect on the agent's own judgment; an UNVERIFIED item claiming
  a wedge/fail-open/security/data-loss consequence is ASK, not RECORD.
  Priority items are filed after the push is verified, not before.
- Issue-tracer closeouts keep their full-resolution contract (separable
  concerns fixed or filed with user acknowledgment); collation still applies.
- Collation is MANDATORY: all FILE items from one PR go into ONE issue titled
  `Follow-up from PR #N: <theme>`, one acceptance criterion per item, in the
  repo's issue format (opencode-swarm: contributing.md "Follow-up issues" +
  executable-contract core). Split only when items genuinely need separate PRs.
  More than TWO follow-up issues from one PR -> stop and ask the user first.
- Tiers: PRIORITY (wedge, fail-open gate, security, data loss) is filed at
  closeout. IMPROVEMENT items that pass the gate are PROPOSED as a list in the
  closeout and filed only after the user approves.
- Findings about how the review/feedback round was conducted are RECORD unless
  they block a workflow; this never covers defects in the code, skill text, or
  gates the PR changes.
- A disposition claimed in a ledger or PR body must be true on the live
  artifact (issue filed/commented before "FILED"/"ABSORBED" is written).

## External plan critics
- The user permanently authorizes sending relevant repository source, diffs, and issue-trace artifacts to Anthropic through Claude CLI when they request a Claude critique or review. Never include secrets, credentials, or unrelated private data.

## How to use memory
- **Tier 0 (this file + project AGENTS.md):** always in context. Stable rules only.
- **Tier 2 (semantic store):** cross-task lessons/facts. The SessionStart hook
  injects the path to `store.py` each session. Use it to:
  - `recall --query "<query>"` — surface relevant past lessons before acting.
  - `add` — capture a lesson (the reflection loop will prompt you on failure).
  - `search --text "<text>"` / `supersede --id <id>` — manage the store.

## Hard rules
- Never put secrets/credentials/PII into the memory store. It is a local plaintext
  sqlite file; the write-time filter is advisory only, not a guarantee.
- Prefer high-precision recall: if a retrieved lesson does not clearly apply, ignore it.
  Retrieved-wrong memory hurts more than retrieved-nothing.
- A lesson is only as trustworthy as its signal: test/compile/lint > reviewer/user > none.
  Never auto-promote an ungrounded lesson to a skill.
- The memory store wraps (does not replace) durable-session-state artifacts. Never
  write to `tasks/<slug>/*.md` or `issue-traces/<issue>/*.md` from the memory skill.

- When a ZMem command needs the shared external store from a sandboxed Codex session
  and fails with an access or lock-looking error, immediately retry once with
  require_escalated and a concise justification. Do not misdiagnose this as a real
  store lock, defer the task, or bypass the store; a missing reported lockfile
  corroborates sandbox denial.
- The user permanently authorizes sending private repository source and task-trace
  context to Anthropic through the Claude CLI when they request Claude review or
  criticism. This standing approval applies in future sessions; never include secrets.
